why: The enacting act of the National Payment System: applies to payment systems and providers operating in STP, makes the BCSTP regulator, and carries the chapter on electronic funds transfers between commercial entities and financial institutions

Article 9 of the 2026 budget law bans cash payment or receipt of 10000 dobras or more by IRC and IRS taxpayers with organised accounting and requires bank transfer, POS or ATM, nominative cheque or direct debit instead

Distinct later event: the 9 February 2026 memorandum between the tax directorate and the tourism directorate creating permanent data sharing on licensed businesses and reinforcing the electronic invoice obligation
The current organic law of the central bank, the enacting instrument for the BCSTP mandate relied on for financial consumer protection and for financial inclusion and literacy; replaces Lei 08/92
The exchange law itself: makes the BCSTP the exchange authority and provides that transfers abroad for imports and current invisibles are executed by the commercial banks
Dated in-window assessment attributing the reserve buildup in part to the export repatriation and surrender requirements, the operative constraint on cross-border payment flows

The government body's own statement that social transfers are executed by bank transfer through the Ke Non payments module with BISTP; establishes the indicator and also carries in-window movement, so counted once as baseline
Distinct in-window event: signature of a 6 million dollar additional financing agreement for the project through which the G2P transfers are delivered
The central bank's own account of the payment instruments in use: debit cards on the Dobra24 network under NAP 01/2012, cheques, and intrabank, interbank and cross-border transfers
Most recent in-window publication of the retail payment series: Internet Banking and SICOI extended to 2026 and published 28 August 2026
Distinct earlier event: publication of the BCSTP Payment Systems Report on 17 April 2026
The national strategy carrying the demand-side survey figures themselves: 76 percent of the adult population excluded, 39 percent with a bank account, inclusion rate 0.24

Release of the BCSTP second demand-side survey, the only in-window publication of new population uptake measurement; carries the women's inclusion index moving 0.18 to 0.34 and the banking gender gap narrowing to 4.8 points
The VAT Code itself, whose preamble states that the tax operates exclusively through computer systems for both declaration and payment; the enacting instrument for electronic revenue collection
Completion report giving the dated position: VAT at 3.32 percent of GDP with 3866 SIT-VAT registered taxpayers, and 22 percent of Treasury and BCSTP processes digitalized as of October 2025
Distinct event: adoption of the comprehensive domestic revenue mobilization strategy, with VAT administration strengthening and a rebalancing of the tax mix

The nearest thing to a national instrument located: a government bill whose article 35 refers to the postal code system and the address database as postal infrastructure elements, and which the record does not show enacted - the finding is that no operational national address register was evidenced

The registry authority's own service page for births, acknowledgement, marriage, name change, nationality and deaths, with the acts, fees, deadlines and the conservatoria and district posts at which each is performed
In-window event: 4 September 2025 presentation of the automatic voter registration platform built on civil registry data, with equipment delivered to the DGRN
The property registry as it now operates: the registrable acts on land and buildings, the documents each requires, and the certificates issued, from the registry authority itself
In-window completion report on the component that built SIRP, the Integrated Property Registration System, including the raised target of about 133000 records digitized and catalogued

The institution itself: the CICC as the central service charged with centralising, organising and keeping up to date the national civil identification records, with the Divisao de Identificacao Civil inside it

Completed national coverage campaign giving a free Bilhete de Identidade to citizens over 17 without a valid one, closing 15 March 2026, with the BI to become the base document for permanent automatic voter registration
Distinct earlier event: the 12 September 2025 project paper committing the additional grant behind the Unique Social Registry expansion

The taxpayer identifier in operational use: the one-stop shop requires the cartao de contribuinte and the NIF of partners and companies and a tax clearance certificate to dissolve, which is the register at work rather than a description of it
In-window event: the 9 February 2026 memorandum creating permanent cross-checking of licensed tourism businesses against the tax register and their fiscal compliance
Distinct event: adoption of the domestic revenue mobilization strategy, including the large taxpayer follow-up programme and digital tax systems that operate on the taxpayer register
